hero.name: Zoya
hero.who: a 22-year-old in Dehradun whose new momo cart near a college stays quiet

story.b: Zoya quit her call centre job to start a momo cart with her brother Faiz outside a college on Rajpur Road in Dehradun. The momos are good. She uses her nani's recipe, with a spicy tomato chutney that makes people's eyes water. But for six weeks, the cart sells maybe thirty plates a day. Across the road, a cold coffee stall opened a month after her. For two weeks it was just as quiet. Then, almost overnight, it had a queue every afternoon. Zoya watches the line of students from behind her steamer. Nothing about the coffee changed. She cannot understand why one stall suddenly took off while hers is still waiting. She starts paying attention to what happened over there.

ask.q: Zoya is puzzled that the coffee stall exploded overnight. What is the most useful question for her to ask?
o: Whether her momos are simply worse than she thinks
What small things tipped the coffee stall from quiet to crowded
Whether she should copy the stall and sell coffee too
ask.why: Doubting her food or copying the menu misses what happened. Nothing about the coffee changed, so something else spread the word. Looking for the small causes that pushed it over the edge gives her ideas she can use for her own cart.

chapters.take: Things often take off suddenly, after small causes quietly build up.

story.b: Zoya buys a cold coffee and chats with the stall owner, a cheerful man named Deepak. She asks how the queue started. He shrugs. One evening during exams, a group from the girls' hostel came for coffee to stay awake. The next evening they brought their roommates. Within a week, cold coffee was simply what you did during exams. Deepak did nothing new. Zoya walks back to her cart thinking. Six weeks of slow sales felt like failure, but maybe it is just the quiet part before things tip. Small causes can have big effects, and change can come suddenly. That night she stops looking up what the cart would sell for. Instead she makes a list of small things she could try.

ask.q: Faiz wants to shut the cart because six slow weeks prove it will never work. What should Zoya say?
o: He is right, slow early sales always mean failure
They should spend all their savings on big advertising boards
Change often comes suddenly, so they should test small triggers before giving up
ask.why: Trends often stay quiet and then take off fast, so six slow weeks do not prove much. Big advertising is costly and may not reach the right people. Testing small, cheap changes looks for the push that can tip the cart into popularity.

chapters.take: Small causes can have big effects. Keep testing before you give up.

story.b: Zoya spends a week just watching the college gate. Some students arrive alone and leave alone. A few seem to pull others along wherever they go. There is Aditi, who organises every fest and seems to know half of Dehradun. There is Kabir, a quiet boy who runs a small local food page and has opinions about every chutney in town. And there is Tenzin, the hockey captain, who can talk his whole team into anything. Zoya does not hand out flyers. She simply invites the three of them, separately, to taste her new cheese momos and tell her honestly what they think. Kabir writes a long post about the chutney. Aditi brings her whole fest committee the next day.

ask.q: Zoya wants more people to know about her new chutney. Who should she tell first?
o: The few people who know everyone, love sharing finds, or persuade others easily
Every student at the gate equally, with printed flyers
Only her family and old school friends
ask.why: Word usually spreads through a few special people: connectors who know many others, mavens who love sharing information and natural persuaders. Flyers for everyone spread effort thin, and family is loyal but small. Reaching the few gets the message moving.

chapters.take: A few people spread most ideas. Find your connectors, mavens and persuaders.

story.b: Students like the momos, but when Zoya asks where they ate yesterday, many cannot remember the name of her cart. It is called Faiz and Zoya Fast Food Corner, which sounds like every other cart in the city. One evening, watching a student fan his mouth after the chutney, Faiz jokes that it should be called the crying chutney. Zoya laughs, then stops laughing. She paints a new board in big red letters: Rona Momos, with a small line underneath saying try not to cry. She sticks a tiny warning flag in the chutney bowl. Within days she hears students at the gate say, chal, rona chalein. The name travels further than any flyer ever did.

ask.q: Zoya's friend runs a tuition centre with a long, forgettable name and a crowded poster. What small change could help most?
o: Add more details to the poster so nothing is left out
Find a short, memorable hook that captures what is special about it
Use a bigger font for the same long name
ask.why: More details and bigger letters do not make a message memorable. A small tweak in how it is presented, a short catchy hook that matches what is special, is what makes people remember it and pass it on without trying.

chapters.take: A small tweak in wording can turn a forgettable message into one people repeat.

story.b: Zoya notices something odd. Afternoon sales are good, but after six the students walk past. She stands across the road one evening and sees what they see. The cart sits in a dim patch between two streetlights. Used paper plates blow around its wheels. There is nowhere to sit. It looks a little sad. So she changes the setting. Faiz rigs a warm yellow bulb on a bamboo pole. She buys a big green bin and two cheap wooden benches, and sweeps the patch twice a day. Within a week, groups start sitting and chatting after classes. They even throw their plates in the bin without being asked. The momos have not changed at all. The corner has.

ask.q: Faiz keeps forgetting to drink water during long shifts, and keeps telling himself to remember. What change would work better?
o: Promise himself more firmly every morning
Ask Zoya to scold him every hour
Keep a filled bottle right next to the steamer where he works
ask.why: Behaviour is shaped strongly by surroundings, often more than by promises or reminders. Firm promises fade in a busy rush, and scolding gets annoying fast. Putting the bottle where his hands already are changes the setting, so the habit happens almost by itself.

chapters.take: If you want people to act differently, change the setting first.

story.b: The paper plates bother Zoya. Hundreds go into the bin every week. She wants students to bring their own steel plates and offers ten rupees off. First she posts about it on a big Dehradun food group with thousands of members. People like the post, and nobody brings a plate. Then she tries something smaller. She asks Aditi's fest committee, eight friends who eat together every afternoon, to try it for a month. They decorate their plates with stickers and tease anyone who forgets. Soon their roommates start bringing plates too. Then the hockey team joins in, because Tenzin cannot stand losing to the fest committee. By December, a stack of steel plates sits on a shelf behind the cart.

ask.q: Zoya wants to start a Sunday clean-up drive in her colony. Where should she begin?
o: With a small, close group of neighbours who care and will push each other
With a big online group of thousands, hoping some will show up
Alone, waiting for others to notice her and join
ask.why: Close groups influence each other strongly, while huge online groups rarely turn likes into action. Working alone can take forever to catch on. A tight group that cares builds the habit and then spreads it outward to friends and roommates.

chapters.take: Start a change in a small, close group. Let it spread from there.

story.b: By the end of the winter term, there is a queue at Rona Momos most afternoons, and it stretches into the evening under the yellow bulb. Kabir's food page calls the chutney the most dangerous in Dehradun, which Zoya prints out and sticks on the cart. Aditi has booked her for the spring fest. The steel plates have their own shelf, and Faiz has stopped talking about selling the cart. Deepak from the coffee stall now sends his customers across the road for momos, and Zoya sends hers to him for cold coffee. One evening, a girl from another college asks Zoya how she made her cart famous. Zoya smiles and says it was mostly small things, done in the right places.

chapters.take: Big shifts rarely need big budgets. They need small things in the right places.
